# Incident Report: Koi Stealer Infection — 2024-09-04

## Victim host

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.17.0.99 | Consistent source of all beaconing traffic |
| MAC | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 | ARP (172.17.0.99 ↔ 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4) and DHCP request from same MAC |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT | NBNS (`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>`, `<20>`), DHCP option 12, DNS PTR queries for `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com` |
| Logged-in user | afletcher | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller 172.17.0.17 |

Domain: `bepositive.com`, DC = `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19` (172.17.0.17, MAC 00:23:ae:50:ba:fd).

## Malware family

**Koi Stealer** — attribution is **signature-confirmed**. The provided Suricata alert export directly names it: `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` fired 48 times on the `172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197` flow, corroborated by `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser` (50 hits) on the same flow.

Behavioral confirmation in the pcap: repeated `POST /foots.php HTTP/1.1` to bare IP `79.124.78.197` on port 80, spaced roughly 60–90 seconds apart from t+155s through t+3565s (the full remainder of the capture), using a spoofed legacy user-agent (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; ...)`) and `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` / `Content-Encoding: binary` bodies. TCP stream 48 shows a persistent bot ID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` sent in each check-in (`101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|...`), classic stealer C2 protocol shape.

A companion gate/loader check-in was also observed: `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` and `POST /index.php` to the same host, with plaintext server response:
```
HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|
```
This is consistent with a pay-per-install loader gate handing off to the stealer payload.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | `79.124.78.197:80` | 48× confirmed `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin` alerts; persistent HTTP beaconing from victim, frames 1668–5077 |
| URL | `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` | Repeated POST target, TCP stream 48 (and many later streams) |
| URL | `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` | POST/GET loader gate, frames 2227/2236 |
| URL | `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` | GET request, frame 2227, server returned bot ID/subid/C2 URL triple |
| Bot ID (session identifier) | `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` | Sent in every `/foots.php` POST body, TCP stream 48 |
| Affiliate/subid tag | `qIOuKk7U` | Present in both the index.php URL and the plaintext response body |

No malware executable or archive was recoverable from the capture: all C2 bodies are binary/encrypted (`application/octet-stream`, `Content-Encoding: binary`), so no file name or SHA256 hash could be grounded in the traffic. The delivery vector could not be conclusively identified — a large (~701 KB) TLS session to `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201) immediately precedes and overlaps the first C2 beacon (TLS session t+153.3s to t+255.2s; first `/foots.php` POST at t+155.9s), which is suggestive of a compromised/malvertising delivery site, but the session is encrypted and cannot be confirmed as the payload drop — flagging it as a lead, not a confirmed IOC.

## Benign context (not indicators)

- `www.msftconnecttest.com` GET `/connecttest.txt` — Windows NCSI connectivity check (also triggered the noisy `ET INFO Terse Request for .txt` / `ET INFO Microsoft Connection Test` alerts as false positives on this benign check).
- `acroipm2.adobe.com GET /assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` — legitimate Adobe ARM update-check ping.
- `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `x1.c.lencr.org` — Windows CTL/CRL revocation list downloads.
- All `*.microsoft.com`, `*.msn.com`, `*.bing.com`, `office*`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `sso.godaddy.com` traffic — normal enterprise workstation telemetry/Office/SSO background noise.
- Internal LDAP/Kerberos/SMB/DCE-RPC traffic to 172.17.0.17 — normal AD domain-join operations (the `GPL NETBIOS`/`GPL RPC` overflow-pattern alerts are generic signature matches on legitimate SMBv1/Kerberos protocol fields, not confirmed exploitation).

## Summary

Windows workstation DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user `afletcher` on the `bepositive.com` AD domain, is infected with **Koi Stealer** (signature-confirmed via ETPRO Suricata rule). Starting at t+155.9s the host began persistent HTTP beaconing to C2 `79.124.78.197:80` via `/foots.php` and `/index.php` using bot ID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` and continued through the entire remaining capture (~59 minutes), indicating active, ongoing exfiltration/check-in traffic at the time the capture ended.
